At the very far end of the corridor, just beyond the beam, a tall motionless silhouette stands in the dark — there, and wrong.
Two faint points of light hang in the blackness down the passage, paired and low, like eyes that have not yet moved.
A strange dark growth spreads across a far wall, pulsing faintly with its own sick light, veins threading the metal.
A shadow falls across a distant doorway, cast by something out of frame, stretching long and then gone again in the gloom.
A distress hologram flickers at the end of the bay — a face, mouth wide, looping silently, cutting to static, then back.
A dark smear trails from the center of the corridor into the far dark, wet-edged, leading somewhere the light does not reach.
Something at the edge of the torch beam — a curved shape, a shoulder maybe, or a limb — gone when the light swings back.
One cryo-pod stands open at the far end of the row. It should be sealed. The interior is dark and slick.
A single luminous spore drifts slowly through the air midway down the corridor, glowing a pale wrong green, trailing nothing.
The claw-marks on the bulkhead door are fresh — bright raw metal beneath, edges still curled, whatever made them no longer here.
Deep in the ventilation shaft overhead, something shifts — a faint rhythmic scrape, irregular, then silence, then closer by one measured beat.
A handprint smeared on the far wall, dark and incomplete, fingers dragging downward toward a floor drain that gurgles faintly.
The motion sensor at the corridor's end blinks a single slow red pulse — one reading, logged, then cleared as if nothing passed.
A section of grating on the far ceiling hangs loose and bent outward, the bolts gone, the dark above it absolute.
Far down the passage a door stands half-open, backlit faintly, and in that thin slice of light a shape seems to lean.
The temperature display beside the airlock reads four degrees lower than the rest of the deck — local cold, unexplained, recent.
Something has been arranged on the floor ahead — three small objects in a loose line, deliberately placed, leading around a dark corner.
At the periphery of the beam, a length of cable or something that is not cable lies coiled against the wall, still.
A low wet sound carries from somewhere behind a sealed bulkhead — rhythmic, almost breathing, too slow to be machinery, too regular to ignore.
One of the overhead lights at the far end strobes twice, catches something pale and tall, then dies and does not come back.
A fine web of dark filament spans the corridor two-thirds down — thin as wire, trembling faintly, anchored to both walls at chest height.
The emergency locker at the passage's end hangs open, contents gone, inner door scored with long parallel marks running deep into the metal.
A faint bioluminescent smear crowns the doorframe ahead — thumb-wide, greenish, smudged as though something passed through low and close and wet.
The far corridor camera feed on the wall panel shows the same hallway — but the timestamp is forty minutes ahead, and something crosses.
At the edge of sensor range, one life-sign blips — stationary, just beyond the next junction — then the reading drops to zero.
